issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter). The template implementation of Stock defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (two parameters) while other methods in the template (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single argument. This parameter mismatch in the template prevents correct compilation and will confuse students implementing SealSaloon, which must call Stock.findStockIngredient(name).
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Stock class to provide findStockIngredient(String) with single String parameter (matching the problem statement and solution). Either rename the existing findStockIngredient(String, boolean) to an overload or add a new single-parameter method that delegates to it (e.g., findStockIngredient(String name) -> findStockIngredient(name, true/false)). Also ensure internal calls (add, take) and student code will compile against the single-parameter signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter), but the template implementation declares findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) with an extra boolean parameter. This mismatch in the method signature forces students to reconcile differing APIs (problem vs. template) and may lead to confusion when implementing or calling the method to locate ingredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by changing the template method signature to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (remove the boolean caseSensitive parameter), or add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing implementation. Ensure behavior (case sensitivity or ignore-case) is documented and consistent with the specification and solution.
